root_idea.summary: The root centers on something being drawn out, slipping away, or separating from its source.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends to offspring as issuing from a parent, rapid movement as going forth swiftly, and material such as wool or feathers falling away. Related derived and idiomatic uses preserve the ideas of separation, succession, and precedence.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic perfect-tense citation form نَسَلَ.
Displayed as the independently attested Quranic noun نَسْلٌ.

senses.definition: To move swiftly; to hasten forth.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction مِنْ كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُونَ, it describes rapid movement forth from elevated ground. The differing contextual renderings “descend” and “hasten” are treated as realizations of this same rapid-movement sense.

A collective noun for descendants or young, applicable in the lexical evidence to human or animal progeny. The Quranic occurrences use it for progeny in a coordinated-object construction and in the possessive phrase نَسْلَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come off or separate from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of wool coming off a camel and of a shirt coming off a person; the examples illustrate separation from an attached source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shed hair, wool, or feathers; specifically, the feathers that fall from birds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for material detached from an animal’s body, including hair or wool and fallen plumage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to reach the time when their wool is about to be shed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived usage describing the onset of a camel’s seasonal shedding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rapid gait, especially the swift gait of a wolf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for fast walking or running, with the wolf’s rapid gait given as a conventional example.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beget one another or descend successively from one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or successive-generation usage: one generation is born from another.
Used as a fixed expression directed against a man, comparable to تَعْسًا وَنَكْسًا.
A rare nominal usage explained by the image of the honey separating from its wax.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To get ahead of or precede a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of one who advances before the people accompanying him.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only Form VIII cross-reference to عَصِيمٌ; it supplies no independent lexical exposition.
The imprecation formula is represented under its fixed expression.
The progeny meaning is represented under the Quranic noun sense.

cautions: The verb is normalized to the perfect-tense dictionary citation form نَسَلَ, although QAC records the active Form I imperfect يَنْسِلُ.
The supplied Form VIII Lane entry is retained only as a pointer-level note and is not treated as an independently explained public meaning.
